newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-SENIOR WINS CLASSIC BY A STROKE FROM NORMAN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SENIOR WINS CLASSIC BY A STROKE FROM NORMAN.

text.p: World number one Greg Norman made a late attempt to win his own tournament on Sunday but failed by one stroke in his bid to overhaul fellow Australian Peter Senior.
Senior shot a final round of 70 to finish on seven-under-par 281 and win the Greg Norman Classic at the par-72 Royal Melbourne course.
Norman fired a second successive round of 69 for a total of 282. He had been two shots off the lead overnight despite a disastrous 75 on Friday.
Senior remained calm despite driving wind and rain to resist Norman's challenge as joint overnight leaders Jerry Kelly of the United States and New Zealand's Michael Long faltered.
Norman, who will take a three-month break to recuperate from a back problem, briefly shared the lead after sinking a long putt for an eagle three at the 14th hole.

Senior replied by birdeying the hole to open a one shot lead which he maintained until the end of his round for his second win on the Australasian Tour after he took the Canon Challenge title in February.
Long finished third on 283 after closing with a 72 while Kelly, playing in Australia for the first time, fell back to fourth place on 285 after a final round of 74.
